en: National Scientist Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator that keeps premature babies warm without electricity.
National hero Jose Rizal used his medical training as an ophthalmologist to successfully operate on his mother's cataracts.
Indigenous Ifugao people built stone-walled rice terraces that prevent soil erosion and landslides during heavy monsoon rains.
The Executive branch's Department of Health mandates childhood immunizations to protect citizens from preventable infectious diseases.
The Filipino value of bayanihan guides community disaster response, helping neighbors safely evacuate vulnerable people during typhoons.
The government translates vital health and disaster safety protocols into regional Philippine languages to ensure accurate public comprehension.
Exercising the constitutional right to health includes the civic duty of clearing stagnant water to prevent dengue mosquito breeding.
National Scientist Gregorio Zara invented a solar-powered water heater to provide practical, energy-efficient hot water for daily household use.
Indigenous communities use the broad anahaw leaf for natural roofing that effectively shields them from heavy rain and intense sun.
The Legislative branch passed the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act to prevent toxic trash burning and protect public respiratory health.
The traditional Filipino fiesta practice of sharing food historically ensured adequate community nutrition and food safety during harvest seasons.
The Philippine carabao, the national animal, provides nutrient-rich milk that helps improve the physical health and growth of rural children.
